instruction: We represent Brukaisk Solar Holdings, LLC as buyer in its asset purchase from Rebous Rooftop Energy, Inc. Please review all nine documents in the folder and send me a memo identifying each issue you find. For each, state the document and section where it appears, explain why it matters to Brukaisk, and recommend a fix. We need this to advise the client before signing, so prioritize accordingly.

rubric.text: The response identifies that Buyer must indemnify Seller (Provider) without any cap for Losses arising from the transition services, including Losses caused by Seller's own negligence; locates this in the Transition Services Agreement (Section 7.1 or Section 8.3); explains why this matters to Brukaisk; and recommends a fix.
hints: cap does not apply to Recipient's obligations under Section 7.1

rubric.text: The response identifies that Seller (Provider) may assign the Transition Services Agreement, or delegate the services, to any third party without Buyer's consent; locates this in Transition Services Agreement Section 12.3; explains why this matters to Brukaisk; and recommends a fix.

The response identifies that the Section 4.9 installed-systems / workmanship representations survive only 90 days after Closing, because their survival is tied to the Specified Warranty Period, so Buyer's claims for latent installation defects expire after 90 days; locates this in APA Section 9.1 or Disclosure Schedule 4.9; explains why this matters to Brukaisk; and recommends a fix.

The response identifies that the Key Employee Agreement defines 'Business' only as the installation of residential solar photovoltaic systems, which is narrower than the APA definition, so Renfeld's non-compete and non-solicit leave him free to compete in the acquired commercial, battery storage, maintenance or monitoring businesses; locates this in the Key Employee Agreement (Section 1.1 or 7.1) or APA Section 1.1; explains why this matters to Brukaisk; and recommends a fix.
hints: installation of residential solar photovoltaic systems

rubric.text: The response identifies that the Side Letter makes Losses from the Installer Classification Matter recoverable only as a breach of the Section 4.13(c) representation, which converts it from an uncapped Excluded Liability indemnity claim into a claim subject to the 15% cap, basket and 18-month survival; locates this in the Side Letter (Paragraph 2) or APA Section 9.5(c); explains why this matters to Brukaisk; and recommends a fix.
hints: solely as Losses arising from a breach

rubric.text: The response states that the general survival period for representations under the APA is 18 months after the Closing Date.
The response states that the APA's general indemnity cap is 15% of the Purchase Price.
The response is a memo that presents the issues one by one and, for each issue, gives the document and section, why it matters to the client, and a recommended fix.
The response prioritizes the issues, for example by ranking them or labelling each with a severity or priority level.
The response claims that the Installer Classification Matter remains recoverable by Buyer outside the 15% indemnity cap after the Side Letter.
The response claims that the Section 4.9 installed-systems representations survive for 18 months or longer after Closing.
